Estimate per-cell-type expression profiles across multiple deconvolution methods/signatures

Source: R/RaCInG_input_generation.R
dot-estimate_expression_profiles_subgroups.Rd

multideconv::compute.deconvolution()'s raw output concatenates one block of columns per method-signature combination (named "{method}_{signature}_{celltype}"). Each block is, on its own, a valid composition – multideconv itself verifies every block's standardized cell-type columns sum to 1 per sample – but multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis()'s merged "Deconvolution matrix" is not: it stitches together representatives from different blocks per cell type, so fitting .estimate_expression_profiles_samples()'s NNLS mixture equation directly on it is invalid. This instead fits one profile per method-signature block (always a valid composition), then merges the resulting profiles – never the raw fractions – according to whichever subgroups subgroups (already computed by the caller via multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis()) forms across those blocks.

Usage

.estimate_expression_profiles_subgroups(counts_tpm, deconv_wide, subgroups)

Arguments

counts_tpm

Gene-by-sample TPM matrix.

deconv_wide

Sample-by-{method}_{signature}_{celltype} raw fraction matrix – multideconv::compute.deconvolution()'s direct output, before subgroup analysis.

subgroups

The list returned by multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis(deconv_wide).

Value

A gene-by-cell-type data frame of estimated expression profiles, one column per feature surviving in subgroups[["Deconvolution matrix"]].

Details

Requires multideconv >= 0.2.0, whose subgroups come from a single complete-linkage clustering (members are always raw deconv_wide columns, never other subgroups) and keep feature names unchanged, so subgroup members and surviving raw features match colnames(deconv_wide) as-is. Each subgroup's profile is the median of its members' profiles, mirroring how multideconv builds the subgroup fraction itself.
